statutory_basis.quote:
Section 44 o f the Airline Deregulation Act o f 1978 (Public Law 95-504)  
directed that the provisions of Section 10 o f the Railway Labor Act, as  
amended, be invoked despite the fact that the National Mediation Board has  
failed to find that the dispute in its judgment substantially threatens to inter­
rupt interstate commerce to a degree such as to deprive a section o f the  
country o f essential transportation service.

establishment_and_qualification.quote:
1-101. Establishment o f  Board. There is established a board o f three mem­
bers to be appointed by the President to investigate this dispute. No member  
of the board shall be pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of  
airline employees or any carrier.

report.quote:
1-102. Report. The board shall report its findings to the President with  
respect to the dispute within 30 days from the date o f this Order.

independent_findings: The complete original contains three separable commands: establish a three-member Presidential board to investigate this dispute; disqualify interested members; report findings to the President within 30 days of the order. There is no express board-termination or records/savings clause in the EO.

The report deadline is not evidence of actual submission or completion. Nor does this original state that actual report submission alone automatically terminates the board. Statutory consequences must be established separately before any end date is selected.

The preamble expressly invokes section 44 of the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978, Public Law 95-504, directing invocation of section 10 of the Railway Labor Act despite absence of the National Mediation Board threat finding. These are concrete statutory references, not speculative general-law gaps. The inspected held packet did not provide either controlling provision or this board actual-report/termination record.

EO12379 section 5 revokes EO12095. The full revoker has no deferred effective date or savings for this target. August 17, 1982 is supported as formal revocation; its inactive/no-longer-necessary preamble makes it especially unsuitable as automatic proof of first cessation.

No affirmative independent continuing obligation is established by the two EO texts. Conversely the expressly invoked statutory framework and actual occurrence record remain unexamined, so a blanket earliest-end/no-residual conclusion is not established.
The ten earlier machine chain actor/date bindings repeat EO12379 section 5 text; those bindings are rejected. This is not a claim to have independently read those ten original actors.

Complete source extracts and recorded matching fixity support the limited formal revocation finding. Page images were not inspected; missing images alone are not treated as a legal blocker. No root retention-job completion is assumed.
